cards.name: Hardware-aware model autoselection
cards.nugget: Estimate per-host tok/s by blending GPU VRAM bandwidth and system-RAM bandwidth weighted by offload fraction, then pick the largest model that clears a target throughput — calibration-checked against measured numbers rather than trusted blindly.
cards.why_now: G1 is a hand-maintained table; this is the exact auto-selection mechanism it asks for, and the fleet is heterogeneous enough to benefit immediately.
cards.first_step: Hardcode the known VRAM/bandwidth specs for each fleet host, write the tok/s estimator, and validate its predictions against 3-4 already-measured model/host pairs before trusting it.
cards.notes: Bullseye for G1. Build, not buy — it's a small estimator that must encode this specific fleet's hardware; an upstream lib won't know your machines. Calibration-honesty is the part that makes it trustworthy.

cards.name: Grammar-constrained decoding for local LLMs
cards.nugget: Constrain the sampler to a formal grammar (GBNF / JSON-schema-derived) so emitted tokens are guaranteed to parse — structural validity by construction instead of post-hoc retries.
cards.why_now: G4's core pain (7B models emit invalid structured output) is eliminated, not mitigated, by constrained decoding — and it's already shipping in llama.cpp.
cards.first_step: Pass a GBNF grammar (or the JSON-schema flag) to the existing llama.cpp endpoint for one structured task and confirm zero parse failures.
cards.notes: Buy: llama.cpp ships GBNF natively and outlines is maintained — reimplementing a constrained sampler is wasted effort. Pairs with c15 for the cases grammar alone can't enforce (semantic, not just structural, validity).

cards.name: Capability-scoped tool tokens
cards.nugget: Issue short-lived tokens that grant only named capabilities (email.read, memory.write) rather than blanket DB access, with an explicit no-bypass doctrine enforced at the tool boundary — least-privilege for agent tool use.
cards.why_now: G3 (no scoped agent API) is currently 'everything is an unscoped agent'; this is the capability-gated surface it names, and it doubles as strong G6 portfolio material on agent safety rails.
cards.first_step: Enumerate the actual capabilities agents use today, then wrap DB/tool access behind a single gate that checks a per-run capability set before any side-effect.
cards.notes: Build — the capability taxonomy is system-specific. Effort is the catch: retrofitting a gate onto already-unscoped agents touches every call site. Also scores for G6.

cards.name: Litestream streaming replication for SQLite
cards.nugget: Continuously stream SQLite WAL frames to a replica/object store for point-in-time recovery and a single-writer replication story without changing the DB engine.
cards.why_now: Genuinely useful as a backup/PITR safety net, but G2 is explicitly noted as substantially addressed by the cockpit-reconcile engine, so the urgency is gone.
cards.first_step: If pursued, point Litestream at the DB for continuous backup/PITR only — not as the concurrency fix, which reconcile already covers.
cards.notes: Buy if at all — Litestream is the maintained tool; never reimplement WAL shipping. Downranked per the G2 note: it doesn't solve multi-writer (it's single-writer + replicas), and reconcile already owns that problem.

cards.name: LLM-as-judge eval harness with pairwise rubric
cards.nugget: Rubric-driven LLM judging plus pairwise comparison and decoy/holdout controls that detect grader gaming — an offline eval loop that can tell whether a change actually improved outputs.
cards.why_now: anton-scout already runs decoy-injection eval; generalizing that into a reusable harness is low marginal effort and prime G6 interview material.
cards.first_step: Extract the existing decoy/holdout eval into a standalone harness that takes (outputs, rubric) and reports a gaming-resistant score.
cards.notes: Build — you already have the decoy-injection pattern in-house; the nugget is generalizing it. The decoy/holdout control is the differentiator vs. naive LLM-as-judge.

cards.name: AutoSwarm AGI Operating System
cards.notes: Pure VC narrative — 'thousands of AGI agents replace your team,' waitlist. No transferable technique; refusing to fabricate one.

cards.name: On-chain RAG with blockchain prompt provenance
cards.notes: Web3 hype bolted onto RAG. Provenance for a solo operator is a local append-only log, not an NFT ledger. No nugget.

cards.name: Disaggregated prefill/decode inference serving
cards.nugget: Split prefill and decode onto separate GPU pools to maximize throughput, transferring KV-cache between them.
cards.notes: Real datacenter technique but explicitly a 10k+ QPS multi-tenant play — wrong context for a solo single-stream operator. Maps to no gap.

cards.name: Multi-region Kubernetes autoscaling for LLM gateways
cards.nugget: Autoscale gateway pods across regions with global load balancing and spot bin-packing.
cards.notes: Scale-only / multi-region enterprise — a direct anti-goal. No local-first relevance.

cards.name: MetaCognition prompt-chaining framework
cards.nugget: A plan → act → reflect → revise loop with a scratchpad: let the model critique and revise its own intermediate output before committing.
cards.why_now: The reflect/revise loop is a legitimate, demonstrable agent pattern for G6 — but it's well-known and the 'metacognition/self-awareness' wrapper is marketing.
cards.first_step: If demoing for portfolio, add a single bounded reflect-revise pass around one existing agent task and measure whether it actually beats one-shot.
cards.notes: Thin nugget under heavy hype. The loop is real and obvious; don't adopt the framework. Reflection also adds calls — watch the G8 cost tension. Low confidence the wrapper adds anything.

cards.name: Mixture-of-Agents layered ensembling
cards.nugget: Stack layers of model calls where each layer sees all prior outputs and aggregates them, trading many calls for higher single-query quality.
cards.why_now: Real technique, but its cost model (many model calls per query) runs directly against G8's token-budget goal for this operator.
cards.notes: Genuine but mis-fit: quality-for-tokens trade is exactly what G8 is trying to cut. Skip unless a specific high-value query justifies the multiplier.

cards.name: Speculative decoding with a small draft model
cards.nugget: A small draft model proposes several tokens that the full model verifies in one forward pass — same output distribution, lower latency under load.
cards.why_now: G4 names timeouts under load; spec-decode cuts local generation latency with identical output, and it's already in llama.cpp/vLLM so adoption is a config change.
cards.first_step: Enable speculative decoding in llama.cpp with a small draft model paired to the main local model and measure tok/s on a representative structured task.
cards.notes: Buy — it's a built-in flag, not a build. Helps latency, not token spend; secondary G8 relevance for local throughput. Gains depend on draft/target acceptance rate, so measure.

cards.name: Prompt caching for reused system blocks
cards.nugget: Mark the stable system/preamble block as cacheable so repeated runs reuse it instead of re-paying tokens and first-token latency on every call.
cards.why_now: G8 explicitly lists 'no prompt/KV-cache reuse' and 'daily digests burn tokens unbounded' — this is the cheapest direct win, especially on the metered T3 (Claude) tier.
cards.first_step: Mark the stable system block of the highest-frequency T3 agent as cacheable and confirm cost/TTFT drop on the next digest run.
cards.notes: Buy/use the provider feature — Claude supports cache_control breakpoints; locally llama.cpp prompt-cache reuses the KV prefix. Near-trivial effort, squarely on G8. Pair with the just-landed usage instrumentation to measure the delta.

cards.name: Transactional outbox on SQLite
cards.nugget: Record side-effects in an outbox table inside the same transaction as the state change; a single writer drains it — exactly-once local job processing with no message broker.
cards.why_now: Gives autonomous builds reliable, idempotent side-effects via single-writer discipline — useful, but G2 is largely addressed by reconcile so it's no longer urgent.
cards.first_step: Add an outbox table to the existing schema and route one autonomous side-effect through a single draining worker to prove exactly-once.
cards.notes: Build — it's a schema+worker pattern, trivially in-stack. Downranked with G2; its real value is job-processing reliability for autonomous builds more than replication.

cards.name: Schema-validated repair for small-model JSON
cards.nugget: On schema-validation failure, feed the validator's specific error back to the model for ONE bounded repair pass instead of a blind retry — cheap, targeted structured-output reliability.
cards.why_now: Directly on G4, and complements grammar-constrained decoding (c2): grammar guarantees structure, repair handles semantic/schema violations grammar can't express.
cards.first_step: Wrap one small-model JSON call with schema validation and a single error-fed repair attempt; cap at one retry and log repair rate.
cards.notes: Build — it's a thin wrapper around your validator. The 'feed the error back, bounded to one pass' is the nugget vs. wasteful blind retries. Best stacked under c2.

cards.name: Embedding-based contradiction surfacing
cards.nugget: Embed a personal corpus locally and use cosine similarity to surface passages that contradict a given claim, ranked by a confidence score — a contradiction layer over notes.
cards.why_now: A clean local-retrieval demo for G6, but contradiction-by-cosine-similarity is weak (similarity ≠ contradiction) and maps to no acute gap.
cards.notes: Real but loosely mapped. Naive embedding similarity finds related, not opposing, passages — needs an NLI/judge step to actually detect contradiction. Low confidence it pays off; mild G6 retrieval-portfolio value only.

cards.name: KV-cache quantization for longer local context
cards.nugget: Quantize the KV cache (e.g. 4-bit) so a model holds more context in the same VRAM, trading a little quality for context headroom on one consumer GPU.
cards.why_now: G8 notes small nodes 'waste context re-sending state'; KV-quant lets those nodes hold more context locally instead, and it's a llama.cpp flag.
cards.first_step: Enable 4-bit KV-cache quant in llama.cpp on a small-VRAM node and check the longer context holds without unacceptable quality loss on a real task.
cards.notes: Buy — built into llama.cpp/exllama. Secondary G1 relevance (fits bigger context per host). Quality hit is task-dependent, so validate before standardizing.

cards.name: SentientOS self-aware agent kernel
cards.notes: 'Genuine consciousness and emotion,' waitlist, replace-your-team. Pure hype; no technique to extract.

cards.name: Decentralized trustless model marketplace
cards.notes: Web3 NFT marketplace narrative. Irrelevant to a local-first solo operator; no nugget.

cards.name: FounderBot autonomous startup-in-a-box
cards.notes: Same replace-your-team agent-swarm VC pitch. No transferable technique.

cards.name: PromptDAO on-chain prompt registry
cards.notes: Tokenized on-chain prompt royalties. A local prompt library is a directory + git; the blockchain adds nothing. No nugget.

cards.name: MetaMind recursive metacognition engine
cards.notes: 'Artificial consciousness' framing over a plan-reflect loop already captured (more honestly) by c10. Duplicate dressed as consciousness — no additional nugget.

cards.name: Multi-region vector index sharding
cards.nugget: Shard a billion-vector index across regions with global query routing and replication.
cards.notes: Real but billion-scale multi-region — wrong context. A solo corpus fits in one local index. Maps to no gap.

cards.name: Kubernetes operator for GPU node autoscaling
cards.nugget: A k8s operator that autoscales GPU pools and bin-packs inference with spot reclaim.
cards.notes: Enterprise-cluster scale, plus a new always-on daemon — double anti-goal for a stable solo daily-driver.

cards.name: RDMA KV-cache transfer across inference nodes
cards.nugget: Move KV-cache between disaggregated nodes over RDMA to sustain datacenter throughput.
cards.notes: Multi-tenant datacenter technique requiring RDMA fabric. No relevance to a local fleet; maps to no gap.

cards.name: Enterprise rate limiting at 10k QPS
cards.nugget: Distributed token-bucket limiter with global quota coordination across regions.
cards.notes: 10k+ QPS multi-region — explicit scale-only anti-goal. A solo operator needs no distributed quota coordination.

cards.name: Per-query model ensembling for benchmark gains
cards.nugget: Run many large models per query and aggregate to squeeze leaderboard points.
cards.notes: Leaderboard-maximization: many calls per query for marginal benchmark points — directly opposed to G8's cost goals. Near-duplicate of c11's cost mis-fit, even less justified.
